messages.subject: R Application for Google Summer of Code 2011 -- action?
messages.subject_clean: R Application for Google Summer of Code 2011 -- action?
messages.body_plain:
Claudia Beleites and I are putting together the 2011 GSoC application for the R Foundation.

Google gives us just over a week to do this.

So far our list of "ideas" at

http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2011

is not very long. Here is a chance to get a good idea implemented. We also want to have
backup mentors in case one of the mentors is unable to carry through. Please either
contact the proposed mentor or add a note (the ideas are on a wiki) saying you are willing
to help out. In the past we've often worked as a team, though Google insists on one name,
likely for administrative simplicity.

And we need to hear soon from interested students. Do let students know about GSoC -- we
suspect many more would come forward if they knew about it.

So the summary of this message is that we need

- idea proposals
- mentor candidates and supporters
- students interested in the ideas (they should contact the mentors)

For reference, the Google Summer of Code 2011 home page is at

http://www.google-melange.com/gsoc/program/home/google/gsoc2011

This may need a google or gmail login. Let the list know if there are difficulties in access.

John Nash

messages.body_plain:
On Wed, 2 Mar 2011, M. Edward (Ed) Borasky wrote:

> There was a lot of talk in the blogosphere last year about performance
> improvements in the R core interpreter and other parts of the R ecosystem. I
> saw a few blog posts with some bottleneck removals as well. Are there any
> mentors / potential mentors with knowledge / interest in this area? I don't
> know what could be done by *one* student in three months, but I think it's
> something a smallish team (two - three) could do.

I do not think that there is any significant interaction between the
blogosphere and the real world of R development, which is done by a very
few members of R core. Some patches were posted to the R-devel list in
2010 IIRC, and most put aside because, although they seemed beneficial on
the submitter's platform, they had side-effects. There are some threads in
which Luke Tierney discussed proposals, and explained why most often
things are much harder to optimise across the platforms on which R runs
(machines, 32/64 bit, versions of gcc, gfortran, etc.) than one might
initially think. If we see incremental improvements, it's usually because
of careful work by central R core members, often Brian Ripley and Luke
Tierney. Careful reading of R-devel usually indicates areas outside the
immediate core engine where input would be welcomed.

Roger

messages.subject: Re: R Application for Google Summer of Code 2011 -- action?
messages.subject_clean: R Application for Google Summer of Code 2011 -- action?
messages.body_plain:
I'd very much suggest that before thinking about changes/improvements in the R
core the first step would be to win one of the R core people as mentor for such
a project.
(Of course, as R is under GPL everyone is free to branch off "his" R but that's
most probably not very efficient and for sure far from being polite.)

An intermediate strategy like e.g. matrixStats could be adapted, too: the
changes go into their own package, and are offered to R core to eventually move
them into the core if they prove to be good. I'd still suggest winning a R core
member as mentor for this.

On 03/02/2011 09:08 PM, Roger Bivand wrote:
> Some patches were posted to the R-devel list in 2010 IIRC, and most put aside
> because, although they seemed beneficial on the submitter's platform, they
> had side-effects. There are some threads in which Luke Tierney discussed
> proposals, and explained why most often things are much harder to optimise
> across the platforms on which R runs (machines, 32/64 bit, versions of gcc,
> gfortran, etc.) than one might initially think.

Which also means that any serious attempt at a "improve R core" (via
intermediate package or directly) needs considerably more computational
infrastructure than "normal" package projects as the code must be tested on as
widespread a variety of platforms/configurations as possible. I don't think the
R core people can be expected to look into possible improvements that were
tested only two or three configurations - the "prevalence" of good suggestions
would be too low.

[However, that sounds almost like an own project: set up a service that tests on
a large variety of systems.]

On 03/02/2011 07:48 PM, M. Edward (Ed) Borasky wrote:
> I don't know what could be done by *one* student in three months, but I
> think it's something a smallish team (two - three) could do.

Just as side info: GSoC requires per student projects. However, it should be
fine if it is separated into independent sub-project. Also google says that two
students working independently towards the same goal is OK.

My 2 ct,

Claudia

messages.subject: Participating in GSoC 2011
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am Pivithuru Wijegunawardana a final year Computer science and
Engineering undergraduate student of University of Moratuwa Sri Lanka.
I am looking forward to participate in GSoC 2011 with R as mentoring
organisation. I looked in to R project ideas for GSoC 2011 and there
are many interesting ideas that I would like to work on.

I have experience in working with R, and using R functionalities in
java via JRI.  I am very much interested in project idea image
analysis for R [1], since I have a sound Java background as well as
image processing. I looked into ImageJ GUI and tried to get an
understanding about the project. But in this project idea page there
are no tests mentioned for this like other project ideas. It will be
really helpful for me to start working on that kind of test earlier on
if you can publish any tests regarding that project if there is going
to be any.

Your suggestions and ideas regarding the project will be really
helpful and looking forward to work with R in this summer.

[1]-http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?
id=developers:projects:gsoc2011:image_analysis

Thank you
--
Best regards,
Pivithuru Wijegunawardana
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
University of Moratuwa
Sri Lanka

messages.subject: Re: R participates in GSoC
messages.body_plain:
Ian,

> How are we handling the project tests? Should students just send
> answers directly to the mentor listed?

I think so:
a) the mentor is the one who can easiest tell whether the answers are
good or not.
b) I set up my tests so that students should get in contact with me and
discuss the tests. The purpose is to get the communication channels
established well before the project really starts.

> Do the tests have any effect on whether the student's proposal will be
> accepted, or are they just there to provide a minimum bar to weed out
> uncommitted applicants?

The second.

> How involved is the mentor usually with the development of the
> student's proposal? (I was working on my own project last year, so was
> a bit more independent than most)

I guess that depends on the student and on the project proposal.

Timo and Seb who are in contact with me are both undergrad students,
Timo even first year. Obviously, they can't be experienced proposal
writers.
And they propose to help with a package I developed. Both points direct
strongly towards student and mentor actually developing the proposal
together.

I'd expect much more independent work at the proposal of a PhD student
who takes GSoC as opportunity to get funding to realize code related to
his PhD project.

Claudia

PS: I sent this on purpose to the gsoc-r list so that Timo and Seb (and
other students) can read it, but the subject really belongs rather to
google-summer-of-...@googlegroups.com

messages.subject: Mentoring two projects?
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

do you think it is possible (and wished by the R community) to mentor *two* projects (with two different co-mentors, though)?
Do you know of any restriction on Google's side?

Actually, I have two motivated candidate students with different skills; one of them would perfectly fit to the project I already proposed (SoRARO), and the other to another project I was thinking of, but which I didn't propose yet.

Of course I definitely do not want to draw any resources from other R projects. However - if I recall correctly - last year we would have had an additional slot which we did not fill up. Above that, I really would not want to put two motivated students into a battle were only one can win; that would be a waste of resources ...

I would be interested into your opinions about that!

Best,
Felix
